correctness.rationale: Theorem is valid for each finite simple H with n≥1, including isolated/disconnected H, odd n, p(H)=0 and n=2 S0. A τ-fixed point has barycentric coordinates constant on rung singleton or horizontal pair edge-orbits. An invariant matching is a disjoint base collection of monomers/dimers, and its union of prism edges extends to a perfect matching by adding all unused rungs. Thus the fixed space is PL-homeomorphic to M(W(H)). For the augmented matching poset, pair each face by toggling the least base vertex not occupied by a dimer; along every reversed Hasse arrow the dimer set cannot increase, and in a fixed dimer fiber the pivot monomer cannot be removed on a directed cycle, establishing global acyclicity. Survivors are exactly base perfect matchings, all dimension n/2−1. Removing the empty-face matching yields one critical vertex and p(H) critical high-dimensional faces, so the integral CW model is wedge^{p(H)}S^{n/2−1} (or point); n=2 gives p+1 disconnected points. The reduced trace follows from fixed-cell Euler/Lefschetz. Independent code, separate from supplied verify.py, enumerated all 75 labeled simple graphs of orders 1..4, plus K3,3, C6 and edgeless 5, checked invariant prism perfect-matching faces against tile faces, complete directed Hasse acyclicity, exact critical dimensions and Euler; 3,332 covers in 75 small graphs and 843+582+75 covers in three others. Finite checks corroborate, do not prove universal case.
